newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to debate Bank Handlowy sell-off next week.
newsitem.headline: Poland to debate Bank Handlowy sell-off next week.

text.p: The Polish government will discuss the finance ministry's plan to privatise the country's largest commercial bank Bank Handlowy SA next week, deputy finance minister Ryszard Pazura said on Monday.

Pazura confirmed that under the scheme about 30 percent of Handlowy's shares would be offered to a group of big investors and 30 percent would be floated on the bourse, both sales likely to be completed by the end of the second quarter 1997.
"We plan two stages, a public offer and (sales to) a group of investors which would take place by the middle of next year if everything goes according to plan," Pazura said.
Asked when the finance ministry's scheme would be presented to the government Pazura said: "It will be next week."
The programme also provides for allotting 30 percent of Handlowy shares to pension funds to be created under the government plan to reform the ailing social security system.

Pazura said the decision on whether to sell Handlowy shares on the bourse first or to start its privatisation by selling the stake to large investors depended on market conditions, notably on how the sale of another bank, Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA, would proceed.
Pazura said the ministry would announce later in December a tender for an adviser who will estimate Handlowy's market value.
Handlowy netted 390.3 million zlotys in this year's first half with a balance sheet total of 10.46 billion zlotys.
